Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Samantha: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Sam Lee, AE at Redwood, and with me is Diego our SE and Liam in customer success. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:15] Priya: Good, thanks. Excited to get this rolling, we've been looking at a few vendors and wanna see how Redwood fits.
[00:00:30] Diego: Great. Quick agenda — we want to map stakeholders, cover the security checklist, runbook expectations, and then talk pilot scope. Sound okay?
[00:00:44] Ethan: Yep, that works. We're trying to get some clarity on costs and perf tradeoffs, like when does Dedicated make sense versus hosted?
[00:01:02] Samantha: Totally. We'll cover that. Curious first — Priya, can you describe the initial use cases and volume?
[00:01:18] Priya: Sure. Two main things: customer-facing chat on the web — low latency required, target p95 under 700ms but ideally 300-500ms for interactive flows; plus embeddings for search, which we batch overnight but also some near-real-time indexing. Scale is small to start — maybe 50k requests/month, growing to a few hundredk in 6 months.
[00:01:44] Miles: And infra wise we do most in our AWS VPC, we'll need VPC peering or Private deployment. Data sensitivity — PII in prompts, so KMS + no retention is a must.
[00:02:00] Zara: SOC2 is required for vendor selection plus audit logs and SSO, we use Okta.
[00:02:12] Diego: Ok, great. On the security side Redwood supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), RBAC, and audit logs. We also have a Private mode for VPC or full on-prem if needed. For SOC2 and ISO docs I'll have Sam share the pack after the call.
[00:02:34] Priya: Quick question — can you pin model versions? We need reproducible outputs for audits.
[00:02:45] Samantha: Yes — pinning and versioned rollouts are supported, plus canary. Diego, correct me if I'm wrong on the rollback story.
[00:02:54] Diego: Right — canary rollouts with automatic fallback to previous version or to a cheaper variant if the new model fails latency SLOs. Also we do prefix and KV caching to improve token costs for repeated context — though that sometimes gets transcribed as "K-V cash" in our internal notes, sorry.
[00:03:22] Ethan: How do you measure token cost? We have to budget for per-token billing.
[00:03:28] Samantha: We provide token-level cost breakdowns in the Console; for pilots we'll send the cost spreadsheet comparing Hosted, Dedicated (reserved pool), and Private with estimated unit economics based on your prompt shapes.
[00:03:46] Priya: For performance testing — what does the baseline look like? We want latency at different sequence lengths.
[00:03:55] Diego: We'll run a performance baseline with your sample prompts and sequence length distribution. Typical baseline includes: 50x concurrent connections, tokenization/seq length samples, p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput numbers. We'll also do a KV cache on vs off run to show improvement.
[00:04:22] Miles: For network — we prefer VPC peering to avoid egress. Is there a guide?
[00:04:30] Liam: Yes, we'll send the VPC peering guide. For Dedicated we can enable private peering and have a private control plane with whitelisted IPs.
[00:04:44] Zara: About data retention — what options? We cannot allow any prompt content persisted outside our control.
[00:04:52] Samantha: Understood. Redwood has no-logging modes and you can opt in to only ephemeral cache with customer-managed KMS. We'll include our retention config doc.
[00:05:08] Priya: Great. On the pilot length — do you recommend a 2-week smoke or a month-long dedicated pilot?
[00:05:18] Diego: For meaningful perf and cost insights, a month for Dedicated pilot is nicer — gives enough traffic to measure steady-state batching benefits. But we can do a short 2-week baseline first to validate integration.
[00:05:33] Ethan: What about SSO? We use Okta and want SAML-based SSO and RBAC. Any gotchas?
[00:05:42] Liam O'Connor: We support SAML/Sso and SCIM provisioning. The main thing is mapping Okta groups to Redwood roles; we'll share the SSO runbook.
[00:05:56] Priya: Are there any limitations on model choice in Private mode? We prefer an open-weights variant for cost.
[00:06:04] Diego: Most curated open models are supported; for on-prem we can support specific builds but there are kernel/quantization constraints. We'll flag any model that doesn't have an optimized kernel for your hardware.
[00:06:26] Priya: Ok — can you walk through a typical onboarding runbook briefly?
[00:06:32] Diego: Sure — Phase 1: access & networking (SSO, VPC peering), Phase 2: sample prompts + baseline perf, Phase 3: pilot capacity (Dedicated reservation), Phase 4: roll to prod with runbook and SLOs, Phase 5: handover. Each phase has checklist items and owners.
[00:06:58] Ethan: Sounds good. For ownership, who will be our primary Redwood contact?
[00:07:03] Samantha: I'll be the AE and point for business; Diego will run the technical pilot; Liam will manage the onboarding timeline and runbooks.
[00:07:12] Miles: Cool. For the baseline tests, what do you need from our side?
[00:07:18] Diego: Sample prompt set (3-5 representative flows), expected concurrency, tokenization examples, and a minimal test harness or API key to hit the endpoint from your test runner. If you prefer, we can run tests from our region to show cross-region latency.
[00:07:36] Priya: We'll share prompts. One note: some of our prompts include PII so we may need sanitized examples first.
[00:07:45] Samantha: That makes sense — send sanitized examples first, then we'll coordinate secure transfer for sensitive tests and recommend Private mode if needed.
[00:08:00] Zara: Any pre-signed NDA or addendum for security posture?
[00:08:05] Samantha: We already have a standard NDA but we can sign a security addendum; I'll follow up.
[00:08:13] Ethan: Can we run a quick cost example? If we have 100k short chat messages avg 60 tokens outbound, what's rough monthly spend?
[00:08:24] Samantha: We'll model it in the spreadsheet — but rough hosted might be higher due to per-token markup; Dedicated amortizes GPU cost so unit cost can decrease as you scale. We'll send numbers.
[00:08:40] Diego: Also quantization recommendations matter — we can suggest q4/q8 profiles to cut inference cost while maintaining quality.
[00:08:52] Priya: On the pilot, will you support A/B rollouts for model quality tests?
[00:08:58] Diego: Yes — we can do A/B routing and automatic fallback if quality or latency regresses. We'll instrument eval hooks.
[00:09:10] Miles: Any compliance for EU data residency? We have EU customers.
[00:09:15] Samantha: Redwood has region routing; we can route EU traffic to EU-hosted clusters and provide data residency controls. We'll include region docs.
[00:09:26] Priya: Ok last thing — timeline. We want to start the pilot early September if possible.
[00:09:33] Samantha: Sounds doable. Action plan: we'll send security pack and SSO/VPC guides by Friday (2026-08-27), Diego will prepare perf/runbook template by 2026-08-30, and Priya will share sample prompts by 2026-08-28. Then schedule the baseline run the week of 2026-09-06.
[00:09:56] Ethan: That works.
[00:10:01] Priya: Quick nit — we had a follow-up Q on observability: do you expose token-level traces?
[00:10:08] Diego: Yes — token-level tracing available in Console, you can link to traces for requests, but PII will be redacted if you enable no-retention.
[00:10:24] Liam: I'll send a shared calendar invite for the baseline slot; who should be on that?
[00:10:30] Priya: Diego, Ethan, Miles, and me.
[00:10:34] Samantha: Great. Anything else?
[00:10:38] Zara: One technical deep dive later — we might do a kernel/quantization session with your runtime folks.
[00:10:45] Diego: Happy to do that. We'll coordinate a technical deep dive if you want to explore on-prem kernels.
[00:10:55] Priya: Awesome. Thanks everyone.
[00:11:00] Samantha: Thanks — recap of next steps in the meeting notes and I'll follow up with docs.
